items.title: Lu-177 PSMA Therapy vs Observation in Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting patients with oligometastatic prostate cancer (limited spread) who have progressed after initial treatment. It compares Lutetium-177 PSMA therapy (Pluvicto) versus observation to see if early treatment can prevent progression to widespread disease while delaying the need for hormone therapy and preserving quality of life.

items.title: Carboplatin, Cabazitaxel, and Abiraterone in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial tested a combination of chemotherapy (carboplatin and cabazitaxel) followed by abiraterone in patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer. The study measured how many patients remained free of PSA or imaging progression at one year, as well as progression-free survival.

items.title: Actinium-225 PSMA Therapy Trial in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial is testing [225Ac]Ac-FL-020, an alpha-emitting radioligand therapy targeting PSMA, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study evaluates safety, effectiveness, and how the drug moves through the body. Alpha-emitters deliver more powerful radiation to cancer cells than current beta-emitters like Lu-177.

items.title: Opevesostat Combinations for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to test opevesostat (MK-5684) alone or in combination with other treatments. The study will first determine safe doses, then evaluate effectiveness. Opevesostat is an investigational drug targeting a specific enzyme pathway.

items.title: AAA817 vs Standard Care After Lu-177 PSMA Progression
items.summary: This phase 2/3 trial is recruiting metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients whose disease progressed after Lu-177 PSMA therapy. It compares AAA817 (an investigational PSMA-targeted treatment) to standard care options. This addresses an important treatment gap for patients who progress after current PSMA radioligand therapy.

items.title: DS9051b in Advanced Prostate Cancer (First-in-Human)
items.summary: This first-in-human phase 1 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to test DS9051b, a new investigational drug. The study will assess safety, tolerability, and early signs of effectiveness. First-in-human studies represent early exploration of completely novel treatments.

items.title: LY4257496 GRPR-Targeted Radioligand for Prostate and Other Cancers
items.summary: This phase 1 trial is testing LY4257496, a radioligand targeting GRPR protein, in patients with advanced prostate, breast, colorectal, and endometrial cancers. The study evaluates safety and effectiveness both alone and with standard treatments. GRPR is a different target than PSMA for radioligand therapy.

items.title: AZD8359 STEAP2-Targeted T-Cell Engager for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial is recruiting metastatic prostate cancer patients to test AZD8359, a T-cell engager targeting STEAP2 protein on cancer cells. The study tests different delivery methods and doses to determine safety and effectiveness. T-cell engagers are immunotherapy drugs that direct immune cells to attack cancer.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan vs Chemotherapy in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to compare ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd, an antibody-drug conjugate) versus chemotherapy. The study measures overall survival and progression-free survival. This represents a novel targeted approach using antibody-drug conjugate technology.

items.title: Lorigerlimab Plus Docetaxel in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial tested whether adding lorigerlimab (an immunotherapy) to standard docetaxel chemotherapy could prolong time before disease progression in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study compared the combination to chemotherapy alone in 150 patients.

items.title: FG-3246 CD46-Targeted Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial is recruiting metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who progressed on one prior hormonal therapy and have not received taxane chemotherapy in the metastatic setting. It tests FG-3246, an antibody-drug conjugate targeting CD46 protein. The study evaluates safety, effectiveness, and drug levels.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone vs Investigator's Choice in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting patients with chemotherapy-naïve metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. It compares xaluritamig (an investigational immunotherapy) combined with abiraterone versus investigator's choice of standard treatments (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone). The primary goal is to compare overall survival.

items.title: ONC-392 Plus Lu-177 PSMA in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial combines ONC-392 (an investigational immunotherapy) with lutetium-177 PSMA therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who have not previously received Lu-177 PSMA. Patients must have progressed on hormonal therapy and up to 2 lines of taxane chemotherapy. The study is no longer recruiting.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide vs Enzalutamide Alone in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who have not yet received hormonal treatments (ARPI) or chemotherapy. It compares the combination of mevrometostat (an investigational epigenetic drug) plus enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone to see if the combination works better.

items.title: Mevrometostat for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial is recruiting men with castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed on prior treatment. The study tests mevrometostat (an EZH2 inhibitor) alone and in combination with enzalutamide. It includes assessment and maintenance phases, with Part 3 currently enrolling patients.

items.title: DS3201 and Ipilimumab for Metastatic Prostate, Urothelial, and Kidney Cancers
items.summary: This phase 1b trial studied the combination of DS3201 (an investigational drug) with ipilimumab (an immunotherapy) in patients with metastatic prostate, urothelial, or renal cell cancer. The study determined safe doses and evaluated side effects. It is no longer recruiting.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not previously received enzalutamide or abiraterone. It compares the combination of mevrometostat (PF-06821497) plus enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone to determine if the combination improves outcomes.

items.title: ENZA-p Trial: Enzalutamide With or Without Lu-177 PSMA
items.summary: This paper discusses the ENZA-p trial, a randomized phase 2 study combining enzalutamide with or without lutetium-177 PSMA therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The research explores the relationship between androgen receptors and PSMA receptors, aiming to optimize treatment combinations for better outcomes.

items.title: Early-Access Lutetium-177 PSMA Programs: Real-World Evidence
items.summary: This paper reviews early-access programs for lutetium-177 PSMA-617 before full regulatory approval, providing real-world evidence in heavily pretreated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. It identifies factors predicting poorer outcomes including low PSMA expression, liver metastases, and poor performance status, helping refine patient selection.

items.title: Lead-212, Actinium-225, and Lutetium-177 PSMA Comparison
items.summary: This preclinical research compares PSMA-617 labeled with three different radioactive isotopes: lead-212, actinium-225, and lutetium-177. The study evaluates radiochemistry methods and laboratory effectiveness of these different approaches. This research supports development of alternative radioligand therapies beyond current Lu-177 PSMA.

items.title: Terbium-161 PSMA After Lu-177 PSMA Progression: Early Results
items.summary: This study evaluated 15 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients treated with terbium-161 PSMA after progression on lutetium-177 PSMA therapy. Tb-161 emits additional low-energy electrons that may enhance effectiveness. The research provides early clinical data on safety and efficacy for this alternative radioligand approach.

items.title: Combined Radium-223 and Lu-177 PSMA in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This case report describes combined treatment with radium-223 (targeting bone metastases) and lutetium-177 PSMA in end-stage metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The dual alpha/beta radioligand therapy was well-tolerated initially but eventually showed progression with dedifferentiated disease, highlighting challenges in heavily pretreated patients.

items.title: Radium-223 After Lu-177 PSMA: Multi-Center Experience
items.summary: This multi-institutional study analyzed 21 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who received radium-223 after lutetium-177 PSMA therapy. Only 19% completed all 6 planned cycles, with most stopping due to disease progression (62%) or toxicity (10%). Significant blood cell toxicity was observed, including grade 3+ anemia (33%) and low platelets (19%).

items.title: Imaging Practices During Lu-177 PSMA Therapy in Routine Care
items.summary: This real-world study of 184 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients receiving lutetium PSMA therapy found that 44% had CT/MRI/bone scans, 34% had PSMA-PET scans, and 20% had no imaging during treatment. Among patients scanned before stopping therapy for progression, only 10% showed progression solely on imaging without PSA rise.

items.title: Lu-177 PSMA in Treatment-Naïve Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This retrospective study examined lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients who had not received prior systemic hormone therapy or chemotherapy. The research evaluated PSA response and progression-free survival in this earlier disease setting, representing a shift from standard third-line mCRPC use.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibition Overcomes Treatment Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research developed dual BRD4/AKT inhibitors to overcome resistance to AKT inhibitor therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Resistance is often driven by elevated c-MYC oncogene expression. The study identified compound 21d as a promising dual-target agent addressing both pathways simultaneously through laboratory testing.

items.title: Sig27 Gene Panel Links Immune Suppression to Prostate Cancer Outcomes
items.summary: This research evaluated Sig27, a 27-gene panel originally developed for prostate cancer, finding it predicts poor outcomes across 21 cancer types including breast cancer. Unlike other gene tests that measure cancer cell division, Sig27 reflects tumor-associated immune suppression involving macrophages, regulatory T cells, and exhausted killer T cells.
